item.title: Microsoft Declares ‘Code Red’ After Historic Outage, Internal Memos Show
item.description: Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft’s engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July.

item.title: Court Approves Bayer $7.25B Settlement Over Roundup Weed Killer Cancer Claims
item.description: Bayer CEO Bill Anderson said in a statement that the court-approved settlement is “a decisive milestone in the company’s strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup litigation.” Roundup has been used on weeds for over 50 years Missouri-based Monsanto debuted Roundup weed killer in 1974 with the chemical glyphosate as its active ingredient. cancer patients asserting the company should have warned people that its popular weed killer Roundup could cause lymphoma, according to a settlement approved Friday by a Missouri judge. For Germany-based Bayer, which denies that Roundup causes cancer, the settlement provides some financial certainty against mounting litigation costs that have led it to contemplate pulling the product from U.S.

item.title: Waymo Recall Prompted by Several Incidents of Robotaxis Entering Closed Freeway Lanes
item.description: Alphabet-owned Waymo said Tuesday its new recall of nearly 4,500 self-driving vehicles in the US was prompted by 11 incidents of robotaxis entering closed freeway lanes since Oct. On Friday, Reuters first reported Waymo was issuing two recalls for its robotaxis over incidents involving closed freeway lanes and manual traffic control. 9 just three days after the company had “updated the approved scope of operation to reduce exposure to closed freeway lanes.” Waymo said there were no collisions or injuries reported from the closed freeway events, adding it is still working on the recall remedy.

item.title: States Band Together During Holiday Road Safety Initiative
item.description: As part of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s (NHTSA) “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” campaign, law enforcement in both states will deter and intercept impaired drivers during the month of December and into the New Year holiday. During the effort, PSP will offer no-cost child passenger safety seat fitting clinics at several locations statewide, with the goal of keeping Pennsylvania’s youngest travelers safe on the road. Officials from the three states are reminding drivers to use their seatbelts, drive sober, and eliminate distractions behind the wheel this holiday season.

item.title: Smarter regulation means understanding the trade-offs
item.description: Good regulation means recognising those trade-offs and using evidence to decide where intervention will make the biggest difference. At our annual Economics Conference , economists, academics, regulators and industry experts came together to explore how smarter financial regulation can support sustainable growth and innovation. That is why economics matters so much to good regulation.

item.title: Startups Are Picking Names That Can Work Even If The Original Business Model Doesn’t
item.description: Then the pendulum swings, and startups defer to simple names that describe what they actually do. Per a Crunchbase analysis of startups 1 founded in the past three years, companies attracting investor interest are largely opting for names that are both distinctive and vague. Examples of this stylistic direction abound among the most heavily funded newer startups.

item.title: AI Bias In HR: Why Polished Work Gets Overrated And What to Do About It
item.description: In today’s world, all professional employees use AI, whether it’s candidates submitting highly polished CVs with 100% perfect fit with your job description to AI-generated work. It reads beautifully and recommends buying a company at what looks like a reasonable price. If I’d asked for a polished take-home assignment and used AI to grade it, I might have hired the better slide editor.

item.title: ESMA proposal to limit cat bonds in UCITS funds leaves investors with greater risk: Plenum’s Grieger
item.description: Building on that critique, Grieger takes aim at ESMA’s risk assessment of catastrophe bond funds in its TRV Risk Monitor 1/2026 , with the manager stressing that ESMA draws attention to retail investor risks it considers particularly concerning, while simultaneously pointing to its proposal to restrict the allocation of catastrophe bonds in UCITS funds to 10%. In a pointed critique of the European Securities and Markets Authority’s (ESMA) push to cap UCITS catastrophe bond allocations at 10%, Daniel Grieger, Managing Partner and Senior Portfolio Manager at Plenum Investments argues that the regulator’s risk assessment relies on isolated loss events while ignoring decades of empirical data and evidence. In the paper, Plenum Investments shared its opinions on the ESMA recommendation, highlighting that catastrophe bonds are a mature asset class that has been successfully integrated into UCITS over a long period of time.

item.title: MS Amlin syndicate gets upsized $150m aggregate retro from Kanata Re 2026-1 cat bond
item.description: The $150 million tranche of Kanata Re 2026-1 Class A notes will provide Syndicate 2001 and sub-entities with protection on an annual aggregate and industry loss index trigger basis, while the covered perils and regions will include U.S. Lloyd’s syndicate 2001, which is aligned with Mitsui Sumitomo underwriting entity MS Amlin, has now priced and secured its first catastrophe bond, with the Arthur Re Ltd. – Kanata Re 2026-1 transaction set to provide an upsized $150 million of multi-peril and multi-regional retrocession, Artemis can report.

item.title: Allied World secures upsized $375m 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 cat bond at reduced pricing
item.description: Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC) has now successfully finalised its third and largest catastrophe bond to secure an upsized $375 million of annual aggregate retrocession from the new 2001 CAT Re Ltd. Allied World Assurance Company, part of the Fairfax Financial group, returned to the catastrophe bond earlier this month for a renewal and expansion of its protection, given that the firm’s $275 million 2001 CAT Re 2023-1 cat bond is set to mature at the end of this year. In our second update, Allied World kept the $375 million upsized target, but lowered the pricing again for each of the three tranches of notes on offer, as the insurance and reinsurance firm looked to further capitalise on market conditions to lock-in well-priced aggregate protection.

item.title: Lower reinsurance costs support improving returns for US homeowners insurers: Aon
item.description: Lower reinsurance costs are helping US homeowners insurers improve underwriting margins and prospective returns on equity (ROE), although catastrophe exposure continues to constrain profitability, according to global insurance and reinsurance broker and risk advisory firm Aon. According to Aon, lower reinsurance costs can improve net underwriting margins for catastrophe-exposed homeowners insurers, while enhanced protection can reduce earnings volatility and the capital required to support catastrophe risk. In its latest Homeowners Return on Equity Outlook report, Aon highlighted that increased reinsurance capacity and stronger reinsurer appetite contributed to double-digit reductions in risk-adjusted catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance pricing across the broader US property market at the midyear 2026 renewals.

item.title: Applied Systems acquires InsurTech Tailwind
item.description: Applied Systems, a global provider of cloud-based software for the insurance industry, has acquired Tailwind, a document and data retrieval InsurTech company, to accelerate integrated artificial intelligence (AI) automation across the assembly line of insurance. Through Tailwind’s AI-powered technology, Applied aims to further automate the retrieval of carrier documents and their intake into its management systems. As part of Applied, Tailwind will accelerate delivery across the three core domains of the Epic Conductor AI platform: operational AI automation, financial AI automation, and connected AI trading.

item.title: WTW appoints Natalie Kenny as North America Builder’s Risk Broking Leader
item.description: WTW, a global advisory, broking and solutions company specialising in people, risk and capital, has announced the promotion of Natalie Kenny to North America Builder’s Risk Broking Leader, based in New York. Since joining Willis in 2022, Kenny has contributed to the expansion of the company’s builder’s risk business across North America. In her new role, Kenny will collaborate with WTW’s regional, industry, advocacy and production teams to strengthen client relationships and further develop the company’s builder’s risk insurance capabilities throughout North America.

item.title: Tornado Hits Parts of South Florida Following Days of Heavy Rain
item.description: An EF-1 tornado caused damage in Delray Beach and Boca Raton but no injuries, marking one of the latest storms that have plagued much of Florida in the last two weeks. That was preceded by massive amounts of rainfall that caused flooding in parts of Florida’s east coast over the past few weeks. Topics Catastrophe Florida Natural Disasters Windstorm

item.title: Police Investigating if Titans’ Football Player Assaulted Lyft Driver Before Crash
item.description: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Florida following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a ride-share driver. Tampa police said in a statement that Harrell was a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento “when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion.” The driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and struck a second vehicle before colliding with a utility pole. “We have permanently banned the rider’s account from the Lyft platform, reached out to the driver to offer our support, and stand ready to assist law enforcement with an investigation.” The 24-year-old Harrell has not played for the Titans this season.

item.title: Australia Bolsters Online Safety Law With Tougher Big Tech Fine
item.description: Wells described the legislation as Australia’s most significant step yet to improve online safety. The sweeping legislation seeks to reduce online harm by compelling digital service providers from social media platforms to AI chatbots to build safety into their products. Wells said in an interview last month that she wants to use the legislation as a step toward working with other countries and establish basic online safety standards, particularly for children.

item.title: Aviva launches Lifetime Pet Insurance via MoneySuperMarket
item.description: Calum Weston, Managing Director, Pet at Aviva, said: "By launching through price comparison websites initially, we can meet customers where they’re already shopping for pet cover, bringing Aviva’s trusted brand to an important channel for customers comparing pet insurance." Sara Newell, Commercial Director at MoneySuperMarket, said: "We’re delighted to partner with Aviva to offer its new Lifetime Pet Insurance exclusively through MoneySuperMarket. Aviva has launched Lifetime Pet Insurance for cats and dogs. The product is sold initially exclusively through MoneySuperMarket, before expanding to other major price comparison websites during 2027.

item.title: BrokerLink acquires two Alberta insurance brokerages
item.description: BrokerLink , a subsidiary of Intact Financial Corporation, acquired two Alberta insurance brokerages in early November. Calgary-based Touchstone Insurance joined on November 1, followed by Medicine Hat-based Reliance Insurance Agencies on November 2. It offers an exclusive course-of-construction insurance program and specialized coverage for churches and charities.

item.title: Supertake raises $20 million
item.description: AI investing startup Supertake has closed a $20 million seed round led by Adjacent, with backing from Union Square Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Nat Friedman, Nikita Bier, Scott Belsky, Guillermo Rauch, Nemil Dalal, and more. Founded in 2026, Supertake allows people to turn their beliefs into investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents. Users can connect their brokerage accounts (Coinbase and Robinhood for now) and explain what they believe in, and Supertake’s AI turns it into an investment portfolio.

item.title: Primerica authorizes $500 million share buyback for 2027
item.description: Primerica announced that its board authorized up to $500 million in common stock repurchases through December 31, 2027. At year-end 2025, Primerica insured more than 5.5 million lives and had about 3.1 million client investment accounts. The board can end the program at any time, and Primerica is under no obligation to repurchase shares.

item.title: Bereaved families need support, not a battle with paperwork
item.description: The FCA reviewed how financial advisers, wealth managers and investment platforms support bereaved families and those handling someone’s estate. Kate Tuckley, head of department, consumer investments at the FCA, said, 'Dealing with someone’s finances after a death should not mean a battle with paperwork. 'Families need clear information and help without needless delays, not fees for advice they no longer receive.

item.title: Kandoo Car Credit Ltd enters administration
item.description: On 23 November 2026, Kandoo Car Credit Ltd (Kandoo) was placed into administration. Kandoo Car Credit (firm reference number 936619) operated as a motor finance credit broker arranging finance for consumers purchasing vehicles from third-party car dealerships. The joint administrators, Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Ltd, are now responsible for Kandoo while it is in administration.

item.title: Most Unicorns Are Worth More Than Their Last Funding-Round Valuations, Crunchbase Estimates
item.description: The more than 1,900 startups on the The Crunchbase Unicorn Board have a combined valuation of roughly $9 trillion, based on their last reported valuations. The valuation model estimates that a select group of 24 companies have gained more than $10 billion in value since their most recent funding rounds. More than 1,100 companies have values that were flat or up to $1 billion higher than their most recent funding valuations.

item.title: Atrium and CRC launch Fractal Re II third-party capital backed reinsurance portfolio at Lloyd’s
item.description: Atrium, a Lloyd’s underwriter that is part of the CRC Group, is set to benefit from third-party capital investor backed reinsurance capacity to support program business from its parent through a new Fractal Re II portfolio deal, arranged with the help of the CRC Risk Solutions division. Bill Goldstein, Vice Chair and Head of Strategic Partnerships, Capacity and Capital Solutions at CRC, explained, “The launch of Fractal Re II reflects our commitment to developing market-leading solutions that strengthen connectivity between insurers, reinsurers and capital, to deliver better outcomes across the insurance ecosystem.” John Fowle, CEO, Atrium, added, “Atrium are delighted to deliver a compelling demonstration of both the strength of the Lloyd’s model and the benefits of our membership of CRC Group to our capital providers.” Rachel Grunert, Active Underwriter, Syndicate 2026, further stated, “The development of the Fractal Re II solution represents a key milestone for Atrium as the first Portfolio underwriting acceptance into Syndicate 2026. “We are excited to be developing our model in line with our plans and ahead of schedule.” For Atrium, this is an effective way to access third-party capital providers to support its reinsurance of a CRC underwriting portfolio, it seems.

item.title: CalPERS highlights growing ILS investments as a use-case in diversification
item.description: The California Public Employees’ Retirement System, or CalPERS, sees its entry into the insurance-linked securities investment market as a use-case in diversification and following its success, the giant pension investor is establishing a program to incubate diversifying strategies of this kind. It now transpires that allocating to insurance-linked securities has provided a well-timed use-case in diversification for CalPERS, as it continues to shift its investment strategy to better suit the recently adopted total portfolio approach. Most recently, on CalPERS activities in investing into insurance-linked securities and third-party reinsurance strategy funds, we reported in September that the combined valuation of its allocations to the ILS asset class neared $2.5 billion at the mid-point of 2026 , an increase of around 70% just in the first-half of this year.

item.title: ILS and alternative capital expanding footprint into DUAE market: AM Best
item.description: In a new commentary, rating agency AM Best has highlighted how alternative capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS) are increasingly entering the delegated underwriting authority enterprise (DUAE) space, with DUAEs utilising sidecars, catastrophe bonds, and collateralized reinsurance to secure capacity when insurers step back. In its latest market segment outlook, AM Best has maintained its stable outlook for the DUAE segment, with the agency citing an anticipated moderation in premium growth amid more disciplined expansion efforts. Private equity capital, for example, continues to flow into the segment, driving mergers and acquisitions, where smaller and less-differentiated players are likely to become acquisition targets,” AM Best said.

item.title: Romero Insurance Brokers rebrands to Gallagher
item.description: Romero Insurance Brokers has officially rebranded to Gallagher, marking the next stage in the broker’s integration following Gallagher’s acquisition of AssuredPartners in 2025. Under the new rebrand, Romero’s teams will fully transition into Gallagher’s UK retail operations. Gary Fletcher, Managing Director of UK Commercial at Gallagher, said: “Bringing Romero under the Gallagher brand is great news for clients and colleagues and demonstrates our commitment to investing in the business for the long-term.

item.title: Lloyd’s appoints Stephen O’Hearn to Council, Fiona Luck to stand down in 2027
item.description: The appointment aims to fill an upcoming open vacancy in the council membership, as Fiona Luck will be stepping down from the Lloyd’s Council at the end of February 2027. Lloyd’s, the London-based insurance and reinsurance marketplace, has announced Stephen O’Hearn as an independent nominated Non-Executive member of Lloyd’s Council, and a member of Lloyd’s Audit Committee, effective 1 March 2027. Sir Charles Roxburgh, Chair of Lloyd’s, commented, “I look forward to welcoming Stephen to the Council of Lloyd’s.

item.title: Marsh to help global airlines strengthen protection with new cyber insurance form
item.description: “Cyber Aviation combines aviation-specific coverage with Marsh’s cyber risk expertise to help airlines strengthen resilience, make more informed risk-transfer decisions, and move forward with confidence.” Cyber Aviation is structured around how cyber losses develop in aviation, offering airlines tailored coverage for first- and third-party exposures such as network interruption and operational disruption, data and privacy liability, regulatory response, and cyber extortion. Global professional services firm Marsh has announced the launch of Cyber Aviation, a comprehensive cyber insurance solution tailored specifically to the aviation sector. Tom Reagan, Global Cyber Practice Leader, Marsh Risk, commented: “Aviation is a uniquely connected environment where cyber events, whether malicious or not, can disrupt an airline’s mission-critical operations and create multi-party loss scenarios.

item.title: Historic Winner of Texas Oil Regulator Seat Wants Faster Permits
item.description: The first Democrat in 36 years to win a seat on the commission that governs the oil and gas industry in Texas said he plans to work with his Republican colleagues to speed up permitting in the state. 3 amid a so-called blue wave that saw Texas Democrats sweep the governor’s office, a US senate seat and a host of down-ballot races in the state. Texas Railroad Commission member-elect Jon Rosenthal said he aims to find ways to incentivize the industry to expand “responsibly” and did not express plans to reduce oil production in the state.

item.title: Texas Manufacturer Earns Lone Star Safety Award
item.description: The Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers’ Compensation (DWC) has renewed the Lone Star Safety Award for WPT Power Corporation in Wichita Falls. To qualify for the Lone Star Safety Award, employers must maintain an effective safety program, keep injury rates below the national average, and have no work-related fatalities in the previous 12 months. The award honors Texas employers whose safety and health programs serve as models for other businesses.

item.title: Wisconsin Regulator Urges Prompt Claims Settlement Processes From July Storms
item.description: 20 reminding insurers that the office expects a timely claims settlement process for property damage losses resulting from the late July storms that hit the state. On July 26, northeast Wisconsin experienced extreme storms, tornado and hail, causing many residents to be displaced from their homes. The bulletin sent out last week urges insurers to promptly respond to pertinent communications from consumers and complete their claims investigation with “all reasonable dispatch.” Failure to adequately respond to claims may constitute an unfair method and practice in the business of insurance under Wisconsin law, the bulletin said.

item.title: Atrium and CRC launch Fractal Re II at Lloyd’s
item.description: John Fowle, CEO of Atrium, said: "Atrium are delighted to deliver a compelling demonstration of both the strength of the Lloyd’s model and the benefits of our membership of CRC Group to our capital providers." Bill Goldstein, Vice Chair and Head of Strategic Partnerships, Capacity and Capital Solutions at CRC, said: "The launch of Fractal Re II reflects our commitment to developing market-leading solutions that strengthen connectivity between insurers, reinsurers and capital, to deliver better outcomes across the insurance ecosystem." Rachel Grunert, Active Underwriter of Syndicate 2026 at Atrium, described the development of Fractal Re II as a key milestone for Atrium, as the first portfolio underwriting acceptance into the syndicate. Atrium and CRC Risk Solutions have launched Fractal Re II, a third-party-capital-backed reinsurance portfolio of property, specialty and casualty risks underwritten via Atrium’s Syndicate 2026 at Lloyd’s, Artemis reported on 23 November 2026. Fractal Re II succeeds the Fractal Re I transaction and will deliver capacity to the Lloyd’s market from a collective of sophisticated third-party capital providers.

item.title: RiverStone International enters legacy transaction with NHBC
item.description: RiverStone International has entered into a transaction with the National House-Building Council (NHBC) covering a portfolio of UK new-home warranty liabilities, Reinsurance News reported on 23 November 2026. Andy Creed, Group President and Group CFO of RiverStone International, said: "We are pleased to announce this transaction with NHBC. It demonstrates RiverStone’s ability to develop tailored legacy solutions around partners’ objectives and was made possible by the constructive, collaborative approach taken by both organisations throughout the process." Paul Turner, CEO of NHBC, said: "This transaction strengthens NHBC’s financial resilience and supports our long-term strategy.

item.title: Clear Group acquires London broker Alexander Miller
item.description: Clear Group, the UK independent insurance intermediary, has acquired Alexander Miller Limited, an independent insurance broker founded in 1992 that operates primarily across London and the South of England. Hampton and the Alexander Miller team will be based at Clear's London headquarters in Monument Street. Alexander Miller gains access to Clear Group's wider resources, infrastructure, insurer relationships and specialist expertise.

item.title: Genworth names new CEO
item.description: Genworth Financial appointed CFO Jerome Upton as president and CEO and added him to its board after Thomas McInerney stepped down to focus on his health. McInerney led Genworth for nearly 14 years. McInerney resigned as CEO effective November 19 and also left the board.

item.title: Voltaire discloses $573,000 in funding
item.description: Voltaire , the startup using AI to draft claims letters for P&C insurers, disclosed that it raised $573,000 from four investors through simple agreements for future equity (SAFEs). The financing follows a $4.2 million seed round Voltaire announced in May 2025. Founded in 2023 and a team of ~15, Voltaire drafts denial letters, reservation of rights letters and other claims correspondence using language from the applicable policy.

item.title: The Hartford files new trademark
item.description: trademark application on November 17 for “The Hartford’s Integrated Employee Protection.” The application is pending and lists July 31, 2026, as the date the insurer first used the mark in commerce. The November application adds The Hartford’s name and cites a first-use date. The Hartford has coordinated workers’ compensation, disability and leave management since 2010, when it launched The Hartford Productivity Advantage.

item.title: Achmea Farm Insurance Partners with AUSVEG
item.description: Achmea Farm Insurance has partnered with AUSVEG, Australia’s national industry body for vegetable, potato and onion growers, to provide risk management information and industry events. The partnership will give growers access to Achmea’s farm insurance expertise and risk management practices from the Netherlands and other agricultural markets. Achmea Farm Insurance entered Australia in 2013 and sells agricultural insurance directly to farmers.

item.title: Allianz UK expands hotel and restaurant coverage
item.description: Allianz UK has launched a hotels and restaurants offering under its Commercial Select policy for UK businesses with annual turnover between £10 million and £1.5 billion. The offering targets independent restaurants, restaurant chains, hotels and conference centres with hotels. It includes property damage, business interruption, employers’ liability, and public and products liability coverage.

item.title: Aviva adds open driving option for minifleet vans
item.description: Aviva has introduced an open driving option for eligible vans under its Minifleet product, allowing businesses to cover drivers who meet policy criteria without naming each person individually. The option is available to fleet-rated businesses with at least three vehicles through Fast Trade or E-Trade. Brokers can still apply vehicle-specific driving restrictions.

item.title: Gradient AI launches underwriting tool
item.description: Gradient AI has launched Sentinel, a group health underwriting tool that uses lab results to identify potentially high-cost conditions before they appear in medical or pharmacy claims. The tool uses the same census information as SAIL, allowing existing customers to add it to their underwriting workflow without adopting a separate system. Sentinel is available as an add-on to SAIL, the company’s group health and stop-loss underwriting platform.
